proofs.proof: map_async first asserts Rust mapped range empty, sets nonempty mapped range, then invokes backend. Failure callback does not reset this range.
Immediate failure invokes callback synchronously before backend emits concrete native error. Callback erases detailed core cause into BufferAsyncError; native scope carries original cause.
Usage, alignment, bounds, destroyed/device checks can reject before native Waiting state. Native success enters Waiting; no public query exposes this state.
unmap resets Rust range first; core Idle emits NotMapped; core Waiting becomes Idle and synchronously invokes MapAborted callback; Active unmaps. Accessible mapped views must already have dropped.
ErrorScopeGuard is !Send/!Sync. pop removes scope immediately; Drop auto-pops and drops future. No need to await pop to end scope.

Native scope stack is current-thread local with std; pop removes matching top scope synchronously and returns ready(error). Drop-only cleanup scope requires no device poll, completion wait, executor or awaited future.
map promise forwards fieldless SDK error; synchronous unmap calls WebGPU and clears SDK cached mapping. Native cleanup scope is not used on browser.
Dropping receiver only cancels oneshot channel, not GPU map request. Sending after receiver drop returns original value; existing callback may ignore this without panicking.

Existing native Wait/Poll/thread::yield_now contain no await/Pending, so safe cancellation cannot occur inside a poll call. A future async yield would return Pending once and becomes a true cancellation point.

state_representation.meaning: No internal map request has been started; no map cleanup. Admission/staging/submit failure returns without mapping.

This operation owns exclusive mapping access to target. Record only ownership and release obligation, not guessed native Pending/Active/Idle. The callback only sends its SDK result and never acquires cleanup state or unmaps.
Mapped views are gone; ownership disarmed before explicit normal release or following fallback cleanup. Never unmap twice.

flows.handling: Scope around immediate map call is native and blocking_validation gated, remains local to this synchronous block. Install request guard before any result inspection, ? or await. Pop map scope before any yield and prefer its concrete native cause over same-operation fieldless callback error. Return primary; fallback cleanup resets Rust state and suppresses only cleanup Validation.
Primary SDK BufferAsyncError remains source. Core may now be Idle; request guard still owns Rust state reset. Scoped fallback native unmap captures secondary NotMapped; it must not replace Mapping.

Keep actual failure as primary; fallback release may abort pending map or release completed map. Drop receiver is not cancellation of native work. No get_mapped_range until successful callback observed.

Drop mapped view first. Disarm request guard before explicit normal unmap to avoid a second unmap during unwind. Normal release follows existing native observation policy; successful exclusive mapping is Active absent external interference. No early output return while mapped.
Drop mapped view before returning primary host copy/admission failure. Fallback cleanup must not replace that error with secondary native cleanup diagnostics.

Blocking operations execute within one future poll; safe cancellation cannot concurrently drop the future while that poll is running. Preserve existing readback Wait. If a later async yield/receiver await can return Pending, guard stays in future state and cleans on drop; no SDK ErrorScopeGuard crosses it.

Request guard drops with owned target retained, calls synchronous unmap (no scope, await or poll). Pending map promise rejects or mapped allocation becomes unmapped. Callback send into dropped receiver is harmless. No promise or stronger device guarantee invented.

policy.recommended: Use a native cleanup-only Validation scope in fallback Drop, including borrowed native contexts. Create scope, unmap, drop scope in one synchronous current-thread block; discard captured cleanup outcome. No block_on/pop-await/device.poll and no stored scope guard. Browser fallback just unmaps.
policy.necessary_exception: Existing WgpuContext prose says disabled blocking_validation means no scope. Public SDK has no reset-map-context-only operation, while native unmap Idle emits Validation. Therefore strict no-scope borrowed cleanup plus nonmasking reset are incompatible. Document narrow fallback-cleanup exception; preserve disabled operation observation, no GPU completion wait, and no synchronous success verdict for borrowed/browser operations.
policy.limits: Scope catches only Validation from fallback cleanup. OOM/Internal/device-lost handling and unrelated SDK panics remain configured device handling. Success normal unmap may use ordinary existing policy; no all-native-error guarantee. No external alias mapping/destroy race guarantee.
policy.guard_installation: For requested Result-error and cancellation paths, installing guard immediately after map_async returns is sufficient if absolutely no ?/return/await occurs first; synchronous callback only fills channel. Arming immediately before map_async additionally protects SDK/device-handler unwind under preconditions. This broader unwind choice must not claim it can distinguish external already-mapped aliases: exclusive mapping is required in either design.
policy.first_failure: Immediate detailed native map cause takes precedence over fieldless callback from same rejected request. After admission, return actual first observed poll/channel/map/copy cause; fallback cleanup outcome is secondary. Cancellation has no return recipient. Do not overwrite an existing primary with NotMapped or MapAborted caused by cleanup.

preconditions: Context device is exact logical device that created target; context queue is paired with device. Same adapter/backend insufficient.
External aliases grant this operation exclusive MAP_READ mapping access and do not independently map/unmap while lease is armed. Private staging allocation already has internal exclusivity.
No creating-device/map-state query, global map lock, callback status lock or provider abstraction is invented. State enum records request ownership only.
limits: No source edits, project execution, tests/cases/helpers/assertions/doctests, scanners, generators, push or CI.
Native-only immediate map scope is conditional on existing blocking_validation policy; fallback cleanup exception is a recommended explicit policy decision, not an undocumented assumption.
This does not clear full lower family, root all13 inventory, producer integrations or final hosted validation.
